lead.title: Cairdac implants its first patients with ALPS, a leadless pacemaker that draws its energy from the heartbeat
lead.deck: Announced on November 25, the first implants of the ASCEND study were performed at Motol & Homolka University Hospital in Prague by Profs. Petr Neužil and Vivek Reddy (Mount Sinai): the still-investigational device is powered by a piezoelectric energy harvester that turns the heart's motion into electricity, instead of relying on a battery whose depletion today forces the implant to be replaced. For this privately held medtech from Antony, France (a €17M Series A led in 2022 by Mérieux Equity Partners, Supernova Invest and Bpifrance), it marks the decisive step from sheep — 3 months of 100% pacing published in Europace — to humans, in a global pacemaker market estimated at $5.5B.

milestone.title: Siemens Healthineers wins the first FDA authorization for a neurofilament light chain (NfL) blood test in multiple sclerosis
milestone.summary: On November 23, the FDA granted De Novo authorization to the Atellica IM NfL assay, developed with Novartis: it measures a protein released into the blood when neurons are damaged, to help evaluate disease activity in adults aged 18 to 55 with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, alongside clinical findings and MRI. The file draws notably on the Swiss MS Cohort (an NfL z-score above 1.5 roughly triples the odds of future activity) and a Swedish validation in 4,341 patients.
milestone.why: It is the first time a blood biomarker of neuronal injury enters routine MS monitoring in the US: an automated, repeatable test that is cheaper than an MRI, creating a new reference regulatory category. The De Novo also opens a 510(k) path for followers — a signal for European startups in blood-based neurological diagnostics (Alzheimer's, stroke, concussion).

deal.thesis: The CVC arm of Spanish diagnostics group Werfen (We Venture Capital) co-leads with Calculus Capital, alongside Illumina Ventures, IQ Capital, Meltwind and Mercia: a syndicate of diagnostics strategics betting that liquid biopsy will monetise first with pharma (early blood-based detection of organ toxicity, patient stratification) before screening. Six big pharmas are already in early access: a path to revenue ahead of the clinical lung cancer test.

brefsEurope.title: Tagomics raises a £10M seed extension, co-led by Werfen's CVC, for its LiquiPath liquid biopsy
brefsEurope.summary: The platform combines epigenetics, cell-type atlases and deconvolution algorithms to identify which tissue circulating DNA comes from, in order to flag organ damage or drug toxicity early. The company, which has raised £19M in total, adds Anthony Vallance-Owen (We Venture Capital) and Robert Hornby (Mercia) to its board and is preparing the clinical evaluation of a lung cancer detection test.

brefsEurope.title: Brainomix shows a plain non-contrast CT predicts final infarct better than CT perfusion, ahead of RSNA
brefsEurope.summary: In a 146-patient multicenter retrospective study of reperfused patients (lead author Kambiz Nael, UCSF), Brainomix 360 Stroke biomarkers — hypodense core volume and edema-adjusted core via net water uptake — were more strongly associated with final infarct volume than conventional perfusion core estimates. An argument for triaging strokes on the baseline scan available everywhere; poster on December 2 in Chicago.

brefsEurope.title: Demant cuts its organic growth target to 5-7% a year and sees the global hearing aid market slowing in 2027
brefsEurope.summary: At its November 24 capital markets day, Oticon's parent lowered its medium-term target from 6-8% to 5-7%, reflecting the growing weight of its hearing care clinics, and expects the 2027 market at the low end of its 4-6% range, held back by the US managed care channel and no recovery in China — alongside at least DKK 3B of share buybacks. A comparable that cools audiology valuations.

brefsIntl.title: Gentuity names Desmond Adler CEO to accelerate its HF-OCT intravascular imaging
brefsIntl.summary: President since 2022 and formerly at Avedro (acquired by Glaukos) and LightLab Imaging (acquired by St. Jude Medical), he succeeds founder David Kolstad, who remains chairman. The company sells a 1.8F imaging catheter that captures 100 mm of vessel in about one second — an 'industrial exit' leadership profile in a segment dominated by Abbott and Philips.

brefsIntl.title: Adenocyte wins up to NIS 13M ($3.3M) from the Israel Innovation Authority for early pancreatic cancer detection
brefsIntl.summary: Its LINFU platform uses low-intensity non-focused ultrasound to collect cells from the pancreatic duct for direct cytological testing. Already used in California, Florida and New York, the technology is set to be adopted by Shaare Zedek hospital in Jerusalem.

word.definition: A miniature pacemaker, about the size of a large capsule, placed directly inside the heart by catheter from the femoral vein, with no pocket under the skin and no wire (lead) between the two — the two main sources of complications of conventional pacemakers.

parts.label: Capsule
parts.role: the complete pacemaker (electronics, electrode, power) anchored in the ventricle wall

parts.label: Power source
parts.role: a sealed battery today, tomorrow a harvester of the heart's own energy

parts.label: Delivery catheter
parts.role: the tool that brings the capsule up the femoral vein and anchors it

how.t: The electrophysiologist advances a catheter from the groin into the right ventricle and anchors the capsule there, with no chest incision or subcutaneous pocket.
The capsule senses the heart rhythm and delivers an electrical pulse when the heart is too slow; it is programmed and monitored remotely, wirelessly.
In current models the battery eventually runs out; new generations harvest energy from the heart's motion (piezoelectric, at Cairdac) or from its electrical activity (at Celtro) to do away with it.

word.why: Leadless pacemakers remove lead and pocket complications, but the leaders (Medtronic Micra, Abbott Aveir) remain limited by their battery and by the difficulty of implanting several over a lifetime. Innovation is therefore shifting to energy autonomy, multi-chamber pacing and wireless resynchronisation: patentable technology building blocks carried by small European and US companies that are natural targets for the cardiac rhythm giants — Cairdac's first patients in Prague are today's milestone.

startups.name: Cairdac
startups.use: Develops ALPS, a leadless pacemaker powered by a piezoelectric harvester of cardiac motion; first patients implanted in Prague (ASCEND study), €17M Series A

startups.name: Celtro
startups.use: Designs a battery-free, leadless pacemaker whose chip harvests energy from the heart's electrical activity through multiple electrodes; still preclinical

startups.name: EBR Systems
startups.use: Its WiSE CRT system, FDA-approved in April 2025, paces the left ventricle without a lead via an ultrasound-powered receiver electrode, alongside an existing pacemaker
